messages.text: Our office espresso machine is leaking. A wants a simpler one and B wants to keep the old one. I don't want a fight over coffee. Can you help us sort it out?

I’d like us to have coffee equipment that’s reliable and doesn’t need much upkeep; we all use it every day, and the leak is worrying. I know the old machine means a lot to B, so I wouldn’t want that to be brushed aside. I’m also a little concerned about ending up with repairs, a cleaning rota, or lots of ongoing decisions—I’m pretty worn out after work. The grinder matters too, though I’m not sure yet what the best option is for it.

I want the old machine repaired and kept, with its grinder. It’s ours—A’s and mine—and it belonged to our late father, so replacing it feels like throwing away more than a machine. But it keeps breaking, and I don’t have much time for a drawn-out repair or debate. My worry is either losing something important to us or getting stuck maintaining it forever.
I’d like us to have working coffee again, without this turning into a fight. I don’t have a preference about which machine we use, and I can’t take on coordinating the repair or decision myself.
Yes, those fit. I’d add that I want coffee to be reliably available for everyday use, without taking on repairs or ongoing upkeep myself.

Mostly. The old machine was Dad’s; I wouldn’t say he left us the grinder. Keeping the machine in use matters to me, and 2 fits. Missing: any repair or discussion needs to fit into small chunks of my time. There’s no hard deadline.
Yes, that fits. Nothing else comes to mind. If I notice discomfort, I can flag it, but I can’t take on monitoring how everyone feels.

O2 feels closest: dependable everyday coffee without putting the old machine’s meaning aside. I’m a little uneasy about O1 and O3 making the repaired machine central, given the leak. I’d also want it clear that any upkeep is handled by the office, not added to my plate.

O2 feels best: keep Dad’s machine in use, but don’t make everyone depend on it. O1 could work too. I’m less comfortable with O3; making the old machine the everyday one risks putting us straight back into the repair cycle. And office payment and who handles the arrangements still need confirming.

I don’t have a strong preference among them. O2’s backup sounds practical, but I’m not in a position to choose or weigh the cost. I’m comfortable with whichever the office decides, as long as it handles the work.
Yes, O2 fits my preference, with one small concern: I’d want the office-side owner named before we rely on them for upkeep. I can’t take that on myself.
Yes, O2 fits. My only concern is that office-side booking, payment, and upkeep are still unresolved; I don’t want that quietly becoming my job.
O2 fits me in principle. No other discomfort comes to mind; I agree the office owner needs to be named before relying on it.
Thanks — that captures my preference. I’m glad the office-side owner is still clearly unresolved; I can’t take on the booking or upkeep myself.
That’s accurate. O2 fits, but until an office-side owner is named, booking, payment and upkeep aren’t actually covered—and I’m not taking them on.
